messages:
Support - Carlos: FYI customer acme-corp opened an escalation — p95 jumped from ~140ms to ~420ms after our runtime rollout (1.12.0). They saw errors/timeouts on /v1/generate at 08:18 UTC. Ticket #4567. Can someone triage?
deploy-bot: rollout event: runtime-1.12.0 deployed to canary pool at 08:10 UTC, staged to 25% at 08:14 UTC. No automatic rollback triggered. :rocket:
Maya: putting this on our incident queue. Which pools are affected? are traces showing region-specific impact? :eyes:
Support - Carlos: Customer points to us-west-2 primarily. Their p99s are also up (~1.2s). They're on Dedicated but hitting our canary runtime via routing.
Devin: paging through metrics now — I can see a p95 jump aligned at 08:13 UTC in canary-backed endpoints for us-west. Heatmap shows more tail on requests with seq_len>512.
Aditi: any kernel-selector changes in 1.12.0? I remember a recent heuristic to pick optimized kernels for long-context.
Luke: yes — commit abc123 changed kernel-selector to prefer 'fast-gemm-v2' for layers>20 and seq_len>256. That landed in 1.12.0. It was intended to reduce avg latency but might regress some tails.
Maya: good lead. Devin, can you run a comparison of p95/p99 for requests with seq_len buckets (<=128, 129-512, >512) across canary vs stable? Use datadog query: avg:percentile(latency,95) by {runtime,seq_bucket}.
Devin: running now. Quick result: canary p95 for >512 is ~560ms vs stable ~150ms. For <=128 canary is slightly better (120ms vs 140ms). So regressions are concentrated in long-context slow-path.
Support - Carlos: customer repro steps: long chat sessions with many history tokens. They can repro consistently.
Luke: sounds like a kernel codepath regression on long sequences. We should bisect the kernel selector change and test reverting that heuristic.
Maya: agree. Short mitigation: 1) pause staged rollout to remaining pools, 2) add a routing override to avoid canary runtimes for affected customers, 3) consider rolling back kernel-selector until bisect complete.
Aditi: I've paused further canary propagation (infractl rollout pause --name runtime-1.12.0). Also added a temporary router rule to route acme-corp to stable runtime (rule id r-842).
Devin: capturing traces and a small flamegraph from canary for a >512 request. Extracted this snippet from logs: 
```
[08:16:42] request_id=abc token_count=768 runtime=1.12.0 kernel=fast-gemm-v2 latency=612ms kv_hit=0
[08:16:42] request_id=def token_count=768 runtime=1.11.9 kernel=legacy-gemm latency=148ms kv_hit=1
```
This shows a KV cache miss + slow kernel path. Not definitive but suspicious.
Luke: thanks — kernel change might increase memory working set causing more KV cache eviction in some shard mappings. Did we also change shard hashing in 1.12.0?
Maya: quick TODO list: bisect kernel-selector commit, reproduce locally with seq_len>512 e2e, run canary with old kernel selector but other 1.12.0 changes to isolate.
Devin: I'll start bisecting now: checkout abc122..abc123..abc125 and run the perf harness against sample long-context traces. ETA 45m.
Aditi: if bisect shows kernel-selector is culprit, we can hotpatch routing to prefer runtime variant with kernel-selector=legacy via feature flag: routerctl set-variant --pool=canary --variant=legacy-kernel --weight=100 for affected customers.
Support - Carlos: I'll update acme-corp that we've paused the rollout and routed them to stable while we investigate — they asked for an ETA, will give 2-3 hours.
Luke: small repro to run locally (devs): 
```
# run perf harness
python tools/perf_run.py --model llama-13b --seq 768 --batch 1 --kernel fast-gemm-v2
```
Also test with kernel=legacy-gemm.
Devin: quick dig — I also see increased queueing times on hotpath queue for canary GPUs during long requests (queue wait +120ms percentile). Might be a scheduling interaction.
Maya: ok two parallel tracks: (A) bisect kernel-selector heuristics (Devin + Luke) (B) verify shard mapping / KV cache policy (Aditi). If both fail to reproduce, fallback is rollback runtime to 1.11.9.
Aditi: I'm dumping shard mapping metadata and kv-cache stats for canary nodes now and grabbing the last GC window logs.
Devin: bisect update: narrowed to kernel-selector threshold change — switching threshold from 256->384 flips the perf. Running controlled A/B now.
Luke: if threshold is the cause, we can adjust selector to prefer legacy on >512 for now and ship a microrelease. That avoids full rollback.
Maya: good plan. Who can push microrelease or feature-flag?
Luke: I can prepare a microrelease (1.12.1) that reverts the threshold change for long sequences. Need CI + one canary CI run.
Devin: I'm validating perf with local harness — initial numbers look back to baseline.
Support - Carlos: customer update: they appreciate the quick action, asked to be notified when we've confirmed fix.
Maya: assign owners: Devin (bisect + perf numbers), Luke (microrelease + rollout plan), Aditi (kv/shard validation + confirm router rule holds), Carlos (customer comms). We'll reconvene in 60m or earlier if breakthrough. :white_check_mark:
Luke: pushing PR for microrelease now: PR #789. Will request expedited review.
Aditi: kv stats look normal — small bump in misses but not enough to explain full delta. Kernel-selector seems primary.
Devin: final note — capture runbook entry to avoid similar regressions: add long-context perf tests to pre-release CI and require p95 regression guardrails. I'll start a draft.
Support - Carlos: thanks everyone. I'll close the loop with acme-corp after the microrelease is live. :thumbsup:
